discovery: Establishing molecular astrophysics: tracing the physics and chemistry of water and molecules from interstellar clouds to planet-forming disks

nominees.name: Ewine F. van Dishoeck
nominees.affiliation: Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, The Netherlands

subfield: Astrophysics / astrochemistry of star and planet formation
motivation: Ewine van Dishoeck turned molecules into precise physical probes of the cosmos. Her quantitative work on molecular photodissociation and excitation, especially the theory of photon-dominated regions, made line spectra usable as thermometers, densimeters and clocks for star-forming gas. She then led large observational programmes with ISO, Spitzer, Herschel (WISH), ALMA and JWST. Together they followed water, ices and organic molecules from cold clouds through protostellar envelopes into protoplanetary disks. They showed where water is made, how it survives collapse, and that much of a planetary system's volatile inventory is inherited from earlier interstellar chemistry. This combined physical and observational framework underlies our modern understanding of how the raw material of planets, and of the Solar System itself, is assembled. Her work has changed our picture of cosmic origins and links astronomy to the conditions that allow habitable worlds.
